Comparative studies: Mesopotamian flood accounts ↔ Genesis 6–9

Contents
  • A. Downloaded / in the repo
  • B. Free to read online (not downloaded)
  • C. Paid / login-gated / library-only (key items to buy or borrow)
  • Notes

Compiled 2026-10-16. Access key:

  • OA-downloaded: open-access, public-domain or rights-holder copy, saved locally.
  • in-repo: already present in a sibling folder under ../.
  • free-web: free to read online but not openly licensed, so not downloaded.
  • login-gated: academia.edu, ResearchGate or similar.
  • paid: publisher or JSTOR paywall.
  • library-only: print only.
  • unofficial copy: a third-party upload exists but its legality is unclear, so it was not downloaded or linked as a source.

"(unverified)" means the bibliographic or access details come from catalogues or search snippets and were not checked against the item itself.

28 G. A. Rendsburg, "The Biblical Flood Story in the Light of the Gilgameš Flood Account," in J. Azize & N. Weeks (eds.), Gilgameš and the World of Assyria, ANES Suppl. 21 (Leuven: Peeters, 2007) 115–127 https://keibi.uni-tuebingen.de/Record/KEI00002305 paid (Peeters). No author PDF was found on Rutgers. Check academia.edu (login-gated, unverified) The strongest case that Gen 6–8 as a unified text follows Gilg. XI in the same order of motifs, with a comparison chart. A critique is on vridar.org (2019)
29 W. G. Lambert & A. R. Millard (with M. Civil), Atra-ḫasīs: The Babylonian Story of the Flood (Oxford 1969; repr. Eisenbrauns 1999) https://www.eisenbrauns.org/books/titles/978-1-57506-184-9.html paid (pb about $39.95) The standard edition of Atrahasis plus Civil's Sumerian Flood Story
30 W. G. Lambert, "A New Look at the Babylonian Background of Genesis," JTS n.s. 16 (1965) 287–300; repr. with postscripts in Hess & Tsumura (eds.), "I Studied Inscriptions from Before the Flood" (Eisenbrauns 1994) 96–113 — paid (OUP/JSTOR; Eisenbrauns) A sober methodological essay against pan-Babylonianism, with the flood as the real case of dependence
31 T. Frymer-Kensky, "The Atrahasis Epic and Its Significance for Our Understanding of Genesis 1–9," BA 40/4 (1977) 147–155 JSTOR (BA) paid (JSTOR); an unofficial copy is on godawa.com Key: the noise and overpopulation motif in Atrahasis ↔ Gen 9 laws (bloodshed) and "be fruitful"
32 T. Frymer-Kensky, "What the Babylonian Flood Stories Can and Cannot Teach Us About the Genesis Flood," BAR 4/4 (Nov/Dec 1978) https://library.biblicalarchaeology.org/?p=69517 paid (BAS Library subscription) A popular version of #31

Rebuttal: Emerton, VT 37–38 (1987–88)

Notes

  • Hebrew: daat.ac.il was not reached by the search engine. Its Hebrew essays on מבול/גלגמש (e.g. Rapaport's) need a manual search on the site. HUJI syllabi exist for courses on "המבול בספרות האכדית", which suggests reading lists (shnaton.huji.ac.il).
  • SOAS Research Online (eprints.soas.ac.uk) no longer resolves. George and al-Rawi, "Tablets from the Sippar Library VI: Atra-ḫasīs," Iraq 58 (1996) 147–190 was OA there. Look for it in the new SOAS repository (soas-repository.worktribe.com), which blocks scripted access.
  • No shadow-library copies were used. The godawa.com uploads (Wenham, Fisher, Frymer-Kensky) are third-party, so they are noted but not downloaded.
